Wait the product is likely the same as second fragment but with F replaced by O-aryl? The substitution reaction: replace leaving group (hydroxyl) with halogen. So forward reaction: starting material has OH, product has halogen. In retrosynthesis, we go from product (halogen) to precursor (OH). So maybe the OH is on the aromatic carbon that is attached to the second fragment via a C-O bond? The first fragment could be phenoxy (COc1...), which is a phenoxy group (aryl-O-CH3).
